The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ### ① Derived judgments

Read on the net diff of `bf8244cb20` against its merge base with `main` (`fccbd9d0d5`; `main` has since moved to `4e2c42f363` without touching any file this PR edits): 8 files, +740/−10. Inputs: card #25078's body and all ten comments, the PR body and file list, the head's check-runs.

1. **The rule, defined once — right.** `csvTextCellNeedsMark` (`export-format.ts`) is the only definition: the text's first character is one of the six leads AND the text holds at least one character outside the numeric-text set (digits, the space, and the six punctuation marks a signed amount with a group separator or a phone number with parentheses is written with; the first character counts). `markCsvTextCell` prefixes one mark (U+0027); `unmarkCsvTextCell` removes exactly one mark when and only when the remainder satisfies the predicate. No second copy of the predicate exists under `packages/` outside the pins (git grep at the head). The character class is a literal set with one digit range and an escaped hyphen, so it holds exactly those seventeen characters and nothing else.
   - **The 56-case table — no boundary mis-sorted.** Counted: 6 leads before a plain word; 6 leads alone (the four that are themselves outside the set marked, the two signs alone not); 9 + 9 set members after each sign; 5 outside-set cases; 8 ordinary business values including the empty cell; 11 code-point neighbours of the six leads (both sides of each, the neighbour the two signs share counted once), every one unmarked exactly as the code sorts it; a leading space and the mark itself as first character, unmarked. Each expected value agrees with the predicate as written, and the table is round-tripped through mark then unmark for every row.

2. **Served answer `GET /api/v1/data/:object/export?format=csv` — right, and exactly as the PR body states it.** `rowsToCsv` derives `textColumns` once per export from `isCsvTextColumn(metaMap.get(f))`; `formatCsvCell(value, textCell)` marks a value only when it is a string AND the column is a text column, before the RFC-4180 quoting (`/[",\r\n]/`), so the quote wraps the mark. The header row is marked with the flag fixed true; a reference display title and an option label arrive from `formatRowCells` as strings in a text column and are marked by the same rule. The raw path: the route starts from an empty map and the schema-read `catch` leaves it empty, so every column is a text column and every string cell goes through the rule. `rowsToCsv` has two call sites (data rows; the zero-row header), both in this route; no other CSV writer exists in `packages/rest/src`.

3. **Text columns by declared type, never by JS typeof — right.** `CSV_NON_TEXT_TYPES` is composed from the spec's `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES` (number, currency, percent, rating, slider, progress, summary), `BOOLEAN_VALUE_TYPES` (boolean, toggle), `CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES` (date) and `INSTANT_TYPES` (datetime), reached through `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`; `packages/spec/**` is untouched. A string in any of those columns is never marked (pinned for six types); a number, boolean, bigint, Date or serialised object is never marked in any column (the `typeof` string arm is the only one that calls the rule). `time`, `formula`, `autonumber`, `json`, the option and reference types are text columns, and a string cell in them is governed by the predicate alone.

4. **xlsx and json export — byte-unchanged, right.** The xlsx arm writes `headerLabel` and `formatRowCells` straight into the worksheet; the json arm writes `formatRowForJson`. Neither calls `rowsToCsv`, `formatCsvCell` or the rule, and the diff touches neither arm nor `formatCellValue`, `formatRowCells` or `formatRowForJson`.

5. **`parseCsvToRows` (published from `packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — right.** Every data cell is read through `unmarkCsvTextCell`; each header cell is unmarked BEFORE `.trim()` and before the inline `mapping[h]` lookup, so an inline mapping names the label as the export labelled it (pinned). The reversal reads the cell text alone and sits before any mapping: the inline rename happens inside this parse by header; a named mapping's `applyMappingToRows` (core) runs after the parse and reads `row[source]` by that unmarked header (pinned through the sync door with a named mapping whose source label begins with a lead).
   - **All three CSV doors — right.** `prepareImportRequest`'s CSV branch is the only caller of `parseCsvToRows`; the sync door (`data-action-routes.ts` about 369), the async import-job door (about 483) and plugin-auth's `runAdminImportUsers` (`admin-import-users.ts` 550, which forwards the `csv` body) all parse through it. The json branches (`format: 'json'` with `rows`, a bare array) call only the inline rename; the xlsx branch calls `parseXlsxToRows`. Both untouched: the JSON and xlsx import doors read no mark.

6. **Round trip — every pinned value returns exactly, right.** Ten values (four marked, five ordinary business values, one user-authored cell that is the mark before a plain word) through the sync door with an inline mapping, the sync door with a named mapping and the async job door (real routes over ObjectQL with better-sqlite3 in memory), and ten names through the admin door whose file comes from the real export route; each case first asserts the file carried the marks on cells and on the header label that begins with a lead, so none passes by the writer never marking.
   - **TAB and CR leaders — stated honestly.** Marked by the writer; a CR cell was RFC-4180-quoted before this change too, so the parse keeps it; `unmarkCsvTextCell` restores the leading character; core's text fall-through (`import-coerce.ts`) then trims under the default `trimWhitespace`, which is what it did to the same two values before this change. With `trimWhitespace: false` the stored value returns exactly. Both pinned in `csv-text-cell-round-trip.test.ts`; both stated in the changeset and the PR body.
   - **The one stored shape — stated honestly.** A stored text value that is one mark followed by a remainder satisfying the predicate: `markCsvTextCell` leaves it (its first character is the mark, not a lead), the parse removes the mark, so it does not return. The changeset, the PR body and the `unmarkCsvTextCell` docblock all state it; the dev measured it one-shot and the reading here agrees. A stored value with two leading marks before such a remainder does round-trip (after one mark the remainder begins with the mark, not a lead), and the parse pin fixes that case, so "that shape" in the changeset is exactly one shape.

7. **Public surface of `@objectstack/rest` — right: nothing added, one published behaviour changed and declared.** `parseCsvToRows` is the only published name whose behaviour moves, and the PR body declares it. The five new exports of `export-format.ts` are not re-exported by `index.ts`, the package's `exports` map serves only `.` from `dist/`, and `files` ships `dist` only, so they are module-internal; `formatCsvCell` is module-private; `rowsToCsv` keeps its signature and is not published. The CSV doors' accept set is unchanged (every cell they accepted they still accept); what they store for one cell shape changes, which is the narrowing ② records.

8. **`data-action-routes.ts` — comment only, right.** The eight added and one removed lines are the route docblock; the sentence it corrects ("the raw stored values stream through unchanged") would have been false for csv after this diff. No doc under `content/docs` or `docs/` states the cell-level contract (`references/api/export.mdx` describes the payload shape and `trimWhitespace` only), so the claim's "docs the change makes false" resolves to that one comment; `Flag docs affected by code changes` concluded success.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/rest`: `patch` — matches what the diff publishes.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 as it stands on `main` (`4e2c42f363`): the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The dispatch order's "BREAKING shipped as minor" was the pre-`f2b6cf230b` rule; the dev's deviation to `patch` is the rule on `main`. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. Step 3's migration clause is not owed: nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO mapping; the ADR-0087 marker's reasoning (no metadata, declaration or stored shape moves) is correct on the diff.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** No spec key, accepted value, metadata type, meaning or default moves; `packages/spec/**` is untouched; the declared-type decision only reads the spec's existing classes.
- **Level of the prose.** The changeset describes the change at the PR's own level (the lead set is "a small fixed set that its consumer interprets", the mark is named by code point, the one lossy shape and the TAB/CR trim are stated, the unchanged formats and doors are listed) and its title line carries `fix(rest)!:`. One imprecision: "What to do" tells an outside reader to apply `csvTextCellNeedsMark` (`packages/rest/src/export-format.ts`), but that name is not published by the package (①.7) and `src/` does not ship, so the pointer is to repository source.
